claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu baseline coating has a relatively coarse-grained microstructure without additional grain stabilization.
A controlled thermo-mechanical treatment can refine the FeNiCrCoCu coating into the nanocrystalline regime.
Optimized short-time heat treatments or minor grain-boundary pinning agents can stabilize the refined grains against high-temperature growth.
The intervention will produce a stable nanocrystalline structure with a high density of effectively pinned grain boundaries.
A fine microstructure provides a high density of grain and phase boundaries.
The stabilized grain-boundary network impedes dislocation motion by acting as a barrier.
Pinned grain boundaries impede dislocation pile-up during high-temperature sliding.
Restricting dislocation motion and pile-up promotes more homogeneous, distributed plastic flow.
Distributed plastic flow reduces localized microscopic deformation.
More homogeneous deformation minimizes stress-concentration sites that initiate wear.
A stabilized nanocrystalline FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower wear rate than the coarse-grained baseline.
A stabilized nanocrystalline FeNiCrCoCu coating will exhibit less localized microscopic deformation than the coarse-grained baseline.
The predicted wear and deformation improvements apply during sliding at 550–600 °C under controlled load in ambient air.
The predicted improvements depend on preventing significant grain growth during high-temperature sliding.
Loss of nanocrystalline stability through grain growth will degrade the anticipated wear and deformation improvements.
A lack of statistically significant reductions in both wear rate and localized deformation relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Extensive grain growth during testing would by itself falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The wear and deformation predictions are explicitly conditional on successful suppression of grain growth, but the falsification rule treats failure to achieve that prerequisite as falsification of the mechanism. Grain growth would demonstrate intervention failure rather than decisively refute the conditional mechanism.
